subject.title: [Bug 6.1] Silent config auto-patch from memory-core + error-message auto-fix breaks all cron jobs on hosts without Docker

question: Should OpenClaw treat `openclaw config patch` invoked through agent host exec or plugin/cron automation as an operator-approved config mutation, or require a new provenance/approval boundary for protected paths?
rationale: The source shows a partial gateway-tool guard plus a separate CLI mutation path, and changing that boundary could intentionally affect trusted operator workflows, plugin setup flows, and agent repair behavior.

options.title: Require explicit protected-write provenance
options.body: Keep human/operator CLI writes working, but add a guard or provenance requirement so agent/plugin/cron-originated protected config mutations cannot silently change exec or sandbox posture.

options.title: Text-only hardening
options.body: Remove protected config assignments from model-visible errors while leaving CLI-through-exec config writes as an intentional trusted-operator capability.

options.title: Keep current behavior
options.body: Document that host exec can run config mutations and rely on operator tool-policy/sandbox choices instead of adding a new boundary.

recommendation.title: Require explicit protected-write provenance
recommendation.body: Keep human/operator CLI writes working, but add a guard or provenance requirement so agent/plugin/cron-originated protected config mutations cannot silently change exec or sandbox posture.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work touches both the sandbox/tool-policy diagnostics and gateway config guard surfaces involved in the decision.
